subject: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView
messages:
From: Evan Roberts <evan.roberts@marineview.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MarineView Legal <legal@marineview.io>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — MarineView is closing security review for our 2027 integrations. Two quick asks: can you provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted OK) and confirm how Redwood treats cloud provider controls (carve-out vs. carve-in)? Our auditors want to know whether AWS/GCP SOC reports can be relied on or if there are carve-outs that leave specific controls to Redwood.

We also need a list of subprocessors with evidence (SOC reports or attestations) and, if possible, a short bridge letter if your SOC period doesn’t cover our desired window through 2027-03-31.

To be explicit: our procurement/legal team needs confirmation on —
- exact audit period on the SOC 2 you will share
- which third-party subprocessors are in-scope and whether their SOCs are provided or referenced
- whether encryption keys/KMS are managed by Redwood or an external KMS (and if there’s HSM/KMS evidence)

Can you confirm a timeline for delivery? Preferably within 3 business days so we can proceed with procurement.

—Evan
Evan Roberts
Head of Integrations, MarineView
evan.roberts@marineview.io
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Roberts <evan.roberts@marineview.io>
Cc: MarineView Legal <legal@marineview.io>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView

Evan — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the items you requested. Quick summary up-front:

- We will attach our latest redacted SOC 2 Type II report (audit period noted in the PDF).
- Redwood treats hyperscale cloud providers (we use AWS in prod) as subservice organizations. Our SOC acknowledges AWS for the infrastructure controls; Redwood’s SOC covers application-level and operational controls. In practice that means some physical/environmental controls are AWS’s responsibility (carve-out), while logical access, change management, and application logging are Redwood’s.
- We maintain a subprocessor inventory; we will provide a CSV with current subprocessors and the available attestation/status for each. For subprocessors that publish SOC reports (e.g., Cloudflare, Datadog), we’ll reference the vendor reports and include mapping where applicable.
- We can issue a bridge letter to cover an audit period gap if our SOC’s end date is before 2027-03-31; I’m attaching a bridge-letter template we can sign and date.

I’m looping in Neha (security) and Lauren (legal) to confirm the specific pieces (KMS/HSM details, Cloudflare status) and to produce the subprocessor inventory and the signed bridge letter.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024_redacted.pdf (redacted), redwood-soc2-bridgeletter-20270413.docx (template), subprocessor_inventory_20270412.csv (stub)

Next steps: please confirm whether MarineView accepts vendor SOC reports + a Redwood mapping, or if you require us to produce vendor reports outright. If the former, we can turn this around in ~2 business days.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
pri_yom.das@redwoodinference.com
From: Evan Roberts <evan.roberts@marineview.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MarineView Legal <legal@marineview.io>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView

Thanks — that sounds promising. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Our auditor needs continuous coverage back to 2027-03-31. If your SOC ends earlier, the bridge letter should explicitly state what controls and time window it covers.
- Please confirm whether Cloudflare is treated as a subprocessor in your stack (we use the CDN for content distribution). If Cloudflare’s SOC exists and you can reference it, that will satisfy a large portion of our network-level controls.
- For KMS: do you manage keys in AWS KMS on behalf of Redwood, or do customers have a BYOK option? If keys are Redwood-managed, auditors want to see KMS access controls and key rotation evidence.

If you can send the redacted SOC + subprocessor CSV and a signed bridge letter (or a draft we can review), we’ll move this to procurement.

Evan
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView

Hi Neha / Lauren — forwarding the thread from MarineView (Evan). Action items:

1) Neha: please confirm the current subprocessor inventory (attach CSV), and explicitly confirm Cloudflare & Datadog SOC availability. Confirm KMS model: we use AWS KMS (customer keys optional for enterprise); provide a one-paragraph description of key management, HSM usage (if any), and where rotation logs live (CloudTrail + internal rotation notes).

2) Lauren: quick check on bridge-letter language (I attached the template). Can you confirm the phrasing is acceptable from a legal standpoint and whether we should add any hedging language about vendor-provided SOCs?

Timeline: Evan requested coverage through 2027-03-31; goal is to get a signed bridge letter and the CSV back to him within 48 business hours if possible.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the delivery and final email to MarineView.

—Priyom
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: SOC 2 evidence: cloud carve-out & subservice mapping for MarineView

Priyom / Lauren — holding notes and confirming items below so we can send to MarineView.

Subprocessors (current, high-level):
- AWS (prod infra) — SOC 2 Type II available (carve-out model: AWS controls physical/infrastructure; Redwood controls application/configuration).
- Cloudflare (CDN) — publishes SOC 2 reports; we reference vendor report for network edge controls.
- Datadog (monitoring) — vendor SOC available; we provide mapping for logging/monitoring controls.
- Sentry (error tracking) — vendor SOC as applicable.
- Segment (event ingestion) — vendor attestation on request; limited scope for specific connectors.

KMS/HSM:
- We use AWS KMS for service keys. For enterprise customers we offer an optional BYOK model using AWS KMS or customer-managed keys in a supported HSM. For standard hosted accounts, Redwood-managed KMS keys are used; access is restricted via IAM roles and CloudTrail logs provide key usage audit trails.
- We can provide a short extract of CloudTrail evidence and our key-rotation policy (redacted) if needed.

Bridge letter:
- We can sign a bridge letter dated 2027-04-13 that states our SOC 2 (audit period X–Y) plus the additional coverage for controls listed in the letter, limited to the shared-responsibility items that Redwood manages. The template Priyom attached is fine — legal may want to adjust one sentence to clarify vendor-SOC reliance.

I’ll attach the subprocessor_inventory_20270412.csv (current snapshot) and suggested mapping references. Once Lauren signs off on the bridge wording, we can prepare a signed PDF and send to MarineView.

—Neha
Director, Security Operations
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
